prompt: The FIRST reference image shows an already approved character from our game. Paint a single full-body sprite of a small robot character for a point-and-click adventure game: Ocko, a small friendly autonomous delivery robot (model 2033) waiting on a pavement in June 2035. It is shaped like an upright hard-shell suitcase with generously rounded corners, about knee-to-hip height of an adult, standing on two large dark grey rubber wheels, one on each side at the bottom. The shell is painted a warm cream white with a sunflower-yellow band around the top lid. On its front face is a dark smoked-glass panel with two simple round glowing light eyes in soft pale blue, and below them a small curved row of tiny glowing pale blue dots that looks a little like a smile. On top: a closed parcel lid with a recessed handle; a thin flexible antenna rises from the back corner and carries a small bright orange triangular safety pennant. No arms, no weapons, no sharp edges, no text, no letters, no logos, no number plate. Cute and non-threatening, like a helpful household appliance. Pose: standing still on its two wheels in a three-quarter view turned toward the right, the same viewing angle as the approved character in the first reference image: its front face with the light eyes is turned about 45 degrees toward the right edge of the image, the near side of its body faces the viewer, both wheels stand on the ground. The robot is centred and fills about 75% of the image height, antenna included. The robot is a game sprite: completely visible from the tip of the antenna pennant to the bottom of the wheels, with green margin on every side; both wheels stand on the same invisible ground line. Even, soft, warm daylight from the front-left, no strong cast shadows, so the sprite fits many scenes. Gently curved, slightly exaggerated cartoon shapes as in classic 1990s adventure games, painted with the same brushwork as the people. Background: one perfectly flat, uniform, pure chroma-key green (#00FF00) filling the entire image, edge to edge, with no gradient, no texture, no floor line, no cast shadow, no vignette, no props and no text. The character must have crisp clean edges against the green, with no green tint, glow or reflection on the character. Paint the character in the game's style. The following style line describes the whole game; apply its brushwork, proportions and palette to the character only and keep the background flat green: Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
